rolePlayScript.text: Scene: Pharaoh's throne room in Egypt. Pharaoh sits on his throne looking troubled. Magicians and wise men stand nearby.
Pharaoh had two strange dreams that no one in all of Egypt could explain.
I had the wildest dreams! Seven fat cows came out of the river — then seven skinny cows came and ate them up! And seven big ears of grain were swallowed by seven tiny ones! What does it MEAN?
Um... I have no idea, your majesty.
Me neither. This is beyond us!
The Cupbearer steps forward nervously.
Your majesty! I just remembered something. When I was in prison, there was a Hebrew man named Joseph. He interpreted my dream — and everything happened exactly as he said!
Bring him to me at once!
Joseph is brought out of prison. He cleans up and changes his clothes, then enters and bows before Pharaoh.
Joseph, I hear you can interpret dreams. No one else can explain mine.
It is not me, your majesty — but God will give you the answer you need!
Pharaoh describes both dreams. Joseph listens carefully, then speaks with confidence.

Both dreams mean the same thing! God is showing you what He is about to do. Seven fat cows and seven full ears of grain — seven years of great harvest are coming! Seven skinny cows and seven empty ears — seven years of terrible famine will follow. God is warning you so you can prepare!
Seven years of abundance... then seven years of famine? So what should I do?

Find a wise man and put him in charge of all of Egypt. Collect one-fifth of all the harvest during the seven good years and store it up. Then when the famine comes, the people will have food and will not starve!
Pharaoh and all his servants were amazed. Where else could they find someone with such wisdom?

Since God has shown you all this, there is no one as discerning and wise as you. You will be in charge of my house — only my throne will be greater than yours! I put you in charge of all the land of Egypt!
Pharaoh places his signet ring on Joseph's finger, dresses him in fine linen robes, and puts a gold chain around his neck.
13 years ago I was a slave. Then a prisoner. But God was with me the whole time — and His plan was greater than anything I could have imagined!
All kids together:
Even when life is hard, God has a plan! Trust Him, don't give up — because what He has for you is greater than you can imagine!
